requirement:
A book MAY contain one standalone `{coverage-index}` directive with an empty
body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. The
preprocessor MUST reject duplicate, unclosed, or nonempty directives outside
Markdown code examples. When the directive is present, `habeas mdbook` MUST
replace it with the report of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.index`. I read the implementation of `marker_ranges` and `populate_in` only to confirm that duplicate detection is a single path across all chapters.

Obligations and the tests that cover them:

- **Valid directive, at least three colons, closed by at least as many.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[directive_fences_and_markdown_examples]` accepts `::::{coverage-index}` followed by a blank line and `:::::`. It asserts exactly one marker range.
- **Closing fence shorter than the opening fence.** The same test rejects `::::{coverage-index}\n:::\n`.
- **Unclosed directive.** The same test rejects `:::{coverage-index}\n`.
- **Nonempty directive.** The same test rejects both a directive with a body and one with arguments.
- **Directive nested in another directive.** The same test rejects the marker inside `req`, `example` and `definition` blocks.
- **Duplicates.** The same test builds a book with two chapters that each hold a directive. It asserts that `populate` fails with "only one". `populate_in` collects ranges across all chapters and errors when more than one is found. A duplicate within one chapter takes the same path, so it needs no separate test.
- **Exemption for Markdown code examples.** The same test shows that backtick fences, tilde fences, indented code, inline code spans and multi-line code spans are ignored. Each yields an empty range list instead of an error.
- **Replacement when present.** `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` runs `populate` on a chapter with a directive. It asserts that the content no longer contains `{coverage-index}` and that it does contain the report text, for example "2/2 (100.0%)". The same assertions are repeated in the later stale and incomplete scenarios.

The content of the report belongs to `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`, which this requirement cites. I did not reassess it here. The MAY (the directive is optional) imposes nothing to check. No FIXME acknowledgments apply, and I found no unaddressed gap.

text: :::{req} index
A book MAY contain one standalone `{coverage-index}` directive with an empty
body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. The
preprocessor MUST reject duplicate, unclosed, or nonempty directives outside
Markdown code examples. When the directive is present, `habeas mdbook` MUST
replace it with the report of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
